A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same theoretical study and are readable throughout. V2's Appendices A-D largely relocate proofs from v1's main text, allowing comparison of the complete arguments.

before.justification: V1 reports mathematical bounds, constructive simulations and algebraic proofs. Empirical findings are attributed to prior work; no original experimental or data-analysis outcomes are reported.

after.justification: V2 and Appendices A-D remain theoretical. Its figures illustrate constructions, and Section 8 suggests future experiments without reporting original empirical outcomes.

M1.justification: Corollary 2 changes the streaming algorithm from updating its lookup pointer immediately within a table to freezing the incoming pointer and committing the next pointer after the table ends. This is a localized algorithmic correction; the generalized SSM recurrence and two-step CoT simulator remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or empirical evaluation scenarios. Function composition and pointer chasing remain theoretical problem families; making the existing canonical encoding explicit does not add evaluated task coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates comparison methods. S4, Mamba and transformer research appear as related work, not experimentally tested baselines.

E3.justification: Neither version reports experimental splits, metrics, training budgets or testing procedures. The revised streaming-memory accounting concerns theoretical guarantees.

E4.justification: Neither contains empirical ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity studies or error analyses. V2's recommendation to study width and precision as separate ablation axes is prospective.

E5.justification: Neither reports repeated runs, seeds, confidence intervals or statistical tests. The retained error-probability threshold of 1/3 is a theoretical guarantee.

E6.justification: No empirical numerical or qualitative results are added, removed or revised. V2's new figures are explanatory schematics; changes to formal resource bounds are assessed under T1.

T1.justification: Theorem 4(A) replaces O(dpL + log n) memory with O(dpL + log T_n), where the newly defined T_n includes thought tokens and need not be polynomial in n. This correction propagates through Proposition 2, Corollary 4 and Appendices C-D. Corollary 2 repairs its correctness argument by freezing each table's lookup pointer. Definition 2 and Theorem 1 also make the canonical encoding explicit. These substantively revise central resource guarantees and proofs.

C1.justification: V1's abstract broadly states that offline CoT does not fundamentally increase expressiveness. V2 limits this claim to the communication lower-bound pipeline and explicitly confines the depth barrier to canonical explicit-table composition, including in the introduction and conclusion. These materially narrow the headline claims, while retaining the principal quantitative lower bound and research themes.

C2.justification: V2 explains that transferring the lower bound requires resource-preserving and stream-order-preserving reductions, and distinguishes generalized constructions from realizable S4/Mamba implementations. It adds limitations concerning vector-valued thought tokens, scan parallelism and computational cost. Section 8 also replaces v1's suggested preference for moderate width and standard precision with an explicit statement that the theory cannot rank practical performance.

D1.justification: No software or data access, hardware, hyperparameters or experimental implementation details are added. The canonical encoding and explicit SSM construction details relocated to the appendices were already supplied in v1; the two-step simulator was also already documented.

R1.justification: The reference list is unchanged. Section 2 nevertheless refines the relationship to existing architectures: v1 describes an abstraction covering all known SSM architectures, whereas v2 presents a common upper-level lower-bound model that abstracts away architecture-specific parameterizations and constraints.

P1.justification: V2 moves lengthy proofs from Sections 4-7 into Appendices A-D and introduces main-text proof sketches and roadmaps. It also rewrites the abstract, expands the discussion and adopts the more explicit post-input/input-interleaved terminology. This substantially reorganizes the exposition.

P2.justification: V1 has no figures or tables. V2 introduces three explanatory diagrams covering forward communication, the gate-and-accumulate construction and CoT token timing, plus a boxed practitioner summary. These substantially expand the visual presentation of the central arguments.

improvement.justification: V2 repairs important weaknesses in the online-CoT analysis: Theorem 4 counts all processed steps in its memory bound, and Corollary 2 prevents unintended repeated lookups within one function table. Its narrower claims and explicit implementation limitations also reduce overgeneralization. Together with clearer diagrams and proof sketches while retaining detailed proofs, these changes substantially improve correctness and interpretability.
